'''Ed John Brady''' (born June 17, 1962) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois Fighting Illini]].

Brady was raised in [[Morris, Illinois]], and attended [[Morris Community High School]],<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bell |first1=Taylor |title=Dusty, Deek, and Mr. Do-Right: High School Football in Illinois |date=July 16, 2010 |publisher=University of Illinois Press |isbn=978-0252077319 |pages=280 |edition=1st}}</ref> where he led the Morris Redskins football team to a state championship.  Brady played for the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]] and was a member of the 1983 team which lost to [[UCLA]] 45–9 in the [[Rose Bowl (game)|Rose Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web |title=1983: A 20th anniversary retrospective on the Illini's Rose Bowl |url=http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/football/2003-10-25/1983-20th-anniversary-retrospective-illinis-rose-bowl-seaso |website=[[The News-Gazette (Champaign–Urbana)|The News-Gazette]]|access-date=12 October 2018}}</ref>

Brady spent 12 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He was selected by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] in the eighth round of the [[1984 NFL draft]], and played for the [[Los Angeles Rams]], [[Cincinnati Bengals]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].  As a member of the Bengals, he played in [[Super Bowl XXIII]] in 1989 in which Cincinnati lost to the [[San Francisco 49ers]] 20–16.  Listed as an [[linebacker]], Brady only played a handful of downs at that position.  He played more than 180 career NFL games as a [[long snapper]].  He was the captain of the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] special teams unit from 1992 to 1995.  He retired in 1996 after failing to make the roster for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].

Following his playing career, Brady became a high school football coach in Irvine, California. He currently is coaching inside linebackers and special teams at [[Lakota East High School]] in Liberty Township, Ohio.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brady gives Morris a part of Super Bowl history |url=https://www.morrisherald-news.com/2016/02/28/brady-gives-morris-a-part-of-super-bowl-history/avkxw5l/ |website=Morris Herald |access-date=12 October 2018 |archive-date=31 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331042740/https://www.morrisherald-news.com/2016/02/28/brady-gives-morris-a-part-of-super-bowl-history/avkxw5l/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Earnest Graham Jr.''' (born January 15, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for eight seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], and was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2003.  Graham became a favorite among Buccaneers fans, coaches, and fellow players for his hard work and team-first attitude.<ref name=henderson10172011/>

After football, Graham became involved in various local business ventures. He also served as the head football coach at [[North Fort Myers High School]] from 2014 until 2018.<ref name="resign"/>  In February 2019, Graham was announced as the new head coach and director of football operations at Evangelical Christian School in Fort Myers, Florida.<ref>https://m.facebook.com/story.php?story_fbid=2228052000588779&id=165224540204879 {{User-generated source|certain=yes|date=March 2022}}</ref>

Graham's son, [[Myles Graham|Myles]], is currently a linebacker for the Florida Gators.<ref>{{Cite web|title='Pressure is a privilege': Myles Graham eager to embrace elevated expectations as a sophomore|url=https://247sports.com/college/florida/article/florida-football-linebacker-myles-graham-sophomore-feature-gators-defense-preview-2025-season-252705095/|website=247Sports|access-date=2025-11-29|language=en}}</ref>
